book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Remote area always allowing for some small possibility?

definitions.meaning: the straight reading: the Australian outback, the far-off empty interior

definitions.text: always allowing for some small possibility?
definitions.meaning: the playful reading: someone who will not say 'never' outright doubles it, as in 'never say never'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a distant region where anything just might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEVER-NEVER is the remote Australian outback; the second half teases the doubled 'never', the refusal ever to rule something out completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The outback of northern Australia is called the never-never, a name for wild country far beyond settlement.

clue.text: Prize set up for this designer?

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for prize is written bottom to top

parts.note: a reward is a prize given for an achievement

explanation.surface: Someone asks which fashion designer a trophy has been arranged for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designer' suggests fashion, but here it is simply someone who draws designs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is literally one who draws, so a draughtsman who sketches plans counts as a designer.

clue.text: Ballet to satisfy? Content's weak

indicators.note: content is what is held inside, so the word for weak sits within the word for satisfy

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to satisfy it
wan means pale and feeble

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether a ballet will please, then judges its substance feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as satisfied or as subject matter; it is really the filling of the word for satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about the swan princess Odette.

clue.text: A female needs to get across? Yield!

parts.note: taken as written
to ford a river is to wade across it

explanation.surface: A woman needing to cross something is urged to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: AFFORD means yield in the sense of provide, as a view affords pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to provide or give, the same sense as a field that yields a crop.

clue.text: Hellish home gets wild around noon

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: the word for wild is wrapped around the noon letter

parts.note: feral means untamed or gone wild

explanation.surface: A household turns into chaos in the middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: N for noon is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal comes from the Latin for the underworld, so it is a direct synonym for belonging to hell.

clue.text: Ships with little time to lose skedaddle

indicators.note: the ships word has to lose its time letter

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships
T is the short form for time

explanation.surface: With the clock running down, a navy hurries away.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle is a jokey word for running away, so to flee is a plain synonym.

clue.text: One may show surprise when elevated

definitions.meaning: the riddle asks for a thing that signals astonishment
a raised brow is the classic look of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: A raised EYEBROW is the stock facial sign of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the arch of hair above the eye is the gesture people make on being startled.

clue.text: Colonial got me excited in terms of studying cricket maybe

definitions.text: in terms of studying cricket maybe

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: these three words supply the thirteen letters that get rearranged

explanation.surface: A colonial grows excited when talking about how cricket is studied.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sport; the cricket here is the chirping insect, which entomology studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomology is the scientific study of insects, and a cricket is one example, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Organisation for enthusiasts providing cool card

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it with moving air
a club is a playing card of the black suit with the trefoil

explanation.surface: A society of devotees hands out a membership card that looks smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' reads as an adjective praising the card, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is a society formed by admirers of a performer or team.

clue.text: See leader's residence

definitions.meaning: a see is a diocese, and its leader is the bishop
the official house of that churchman

explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb, an instruction to look; it is the noun for a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: The official home of the bishop who heads a diocese is traditionally called his palace.

clue.text: Weak? Do not get involved with this!

definitions.text: Weak? Do not get involved with this!

indicators.note: to get involved is to become tangled up, so the letters of weak and do not are intertwined into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to feeble people: stay away from this pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of WEAK DO NOT rearrange to the martial art, and a weakling is advised to keep clear of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a demanding Korean martial art of kicks and strikes, so a feeble person is wisely warned off it.

clue.text: Two can go into them with nothing remaining

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a couple squeezing into a space; it is arithmetic about numbers divisible by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Even numbers are exactly those divisible by two with no remainder.

clue.text: Large building needs staff and soldiers

parts.note: to man something is to staff it with people
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A big building has to be supplied with workers and troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house, the main residence on a landed estate.

clue.text: Movement quite slow with worker in love

parts.note: and joins things together just as with does
an ant is the classic worker insect
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sluggish movement happens when a labourer falls in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking for a passage at a moderately slow walking pace.

clue.text: Like a type of article that's not clear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grammatical kind of article, 'a' or 'an'

explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'an' are the indefinite articles of English grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the grammar class of 'a' and also means vague or undecided.

clue.text: Look very competent winning

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
able means capable

explanation.surface: Someone appears highly skilled when coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning' is a victory in the surface, but here it is an adjective for charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is a charming, endearing one, so winning is a synonym for easy to love.

clue.text: Wretched crooner gets to join in

indicators.note: the word for join goes in among the crooner's letters

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the famous crooning singer
to link is to join

explanation.surface: A miserable singer manages to take part.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby is the crooner every setter reaches for.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinking is a mild British euphemism for bloody, used to curse something as annoying or wretched.

clue.text: Swords sold to character at end of battle in special deal

indicators.note: a special deal rearranges the letters, dealing them out anew

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: character means letter, here the last letter of the word battle

parts.note: the final letter of this word is the one taken

explanation.surface: Swords are sold to the hero at the end of a battle as part of a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo in Spain was famous for its sword-making, so its blades are called toledos.
explanation.definitionFit: A toledo is a fine sword forged in the Spanish city renowned for its steel blades.

clue.text: Ground rent-free, big plant provided

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of this hyphenated word are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: Land free of rent is offered, provided a large plant comes with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like land; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large fern with a tall trunk-like stem, so it is a big plant.

clue.text: Someone given legal advice about money — he is wild with anger

definitions.text: Someone given legal advice about money

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control into a new order

parts.note: these two words give four of the letters to be rearranged
this word gives the remaining five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A client hears the lawyer's verdict on their finances and flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: A GARNISHEE is a person served with a court notice to hand over money owed to a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a garnishee receives formal notice concerning money held, to be paid to a creditor.

clue.text: Poet's house overlooking the Channel

definitions.note: read as 'Poet is', so a poet's name defines it

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the house letters above the channel word

parts.note: a race is a channel of water, as in a mill race

explanation.surface: A writer's home looks out over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' reads as possessive but stands for 'Poet is'; 'the Channel' looks like the sea between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was the great Roman lyric poet of the Odes, so he is a poet by name.

clue.text: Criminal group about to get first-class celebrity cut down

indicators.note: about turns round the whole collection that follows

parts.note: AI, A1, is the mark for first-class

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing the last letter

parts.note: fame is celebrity

explanation.surface: A gang is about to fell a top-class star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; 'about' alone is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the organised crime syndicate of Sicilian origin, the archetypal criminal group.

clue.text: What fictional detective without love becomes?

definitions.text: What fictional detective without love becomes?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the detective goes around the love letter

parts.note: Inspector Morse, Colin Dexter's Oxford detective
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a famous detective turns out when deprived of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking but means outside; Morse is famously gloomy and lonely in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective deprived of love would be sullen and gloomy, and morose means exactly that.

clue.text: Rebuke Bill in the restaurant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reprove or restrain them
second meaning: in America the ... is the bill for a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures complaining about the bill; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a reprimand, and is also the American name for a restaurant bill.

clue.text: Drug has reduced pain in a head

parts.note: E is ecstasy

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the pain word loses its last letter

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A medicine has eased a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' reads as part of the body; it is the price phrase meaning per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickets at five pounds a head cost five pounds each, so the phrase means per person.

clue.text: Voting arrangements that could make Dane freer

indicators.note: the letters could be made into something else, rearranged

parts.note: these two words give the nine letters that get rearranged

explanation.surface: A political reform might give a Danish citizen more freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, the plural of referendum.

clue.text: American city figure using few words

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a conic is a conic section, a geometric figure such as an ellipse

explanation.surface: A notable person in an American city speaks tersely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a person; it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means terse, after the Spartans of Laconia, famed for brief speech.

clue.text: Decoration put in rubbish (garbage ultimately)

indicators.note: put goes into the word for rubbish

parts.note: rot means nonsense
to set something is to put it down

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of garbage

parts.note: the final letter of this word closes the answer

explanation.surface: An ornament gets thrown in the bin with the rest of the garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize or worn as a decoration.
